scope.task_definition: Rank 20 km Earth windows by morphometric similarity to a 20 km Jezero window, using 80 km context and four descriptor groups: slope, relief position, roughness/organization, and multiscale context.
scope.question: Is there a public prior association for any of the six exact 20 km candidate footprints, or for the exact terrain-ranking task?
scope.exact_footprint_definition: A published or publicly documented 20 km square at the candidate center, or an equivalent polygon matching the project bounding box.
scope.exact_task_definition: Task-specific regional geomorphological analogue mapping from Earth to Jezero; a change of grid spacing, weights or candidate IDs alone cannot establish scientific novelty.
outside_scope: Field validation or new sample collection
Proof that no prior association exists anywhere

method.inspection_level: Public pages, bibliographic metadata, and abstracts. No paywalled full text was read.
method.exact_string_policy: Exact-string results were used as evidence only where the engine honored quotes and returned an interpretable result. Bing results were not used as exact-string zero evidence because quotes were not honored. OpenAlex and Crossref counts are bibliographic and tokenized, not exhaustive full-text searches.
method.language_coverage: English and Spanish project/agency pages. No systematic Spanish-language literature search.
method.peer_review_policy: Project pages, agency pages, conference abstracts, preprints, and datasets are labeled as such. Peer-review status was not inferred.
method.parent_verification: Parent checked the Cussen author page, NASA overview and original smectite paper; DOI metadata checked through Crossref for Namib dune, Chilean salars and Atacama-Jezero clay work. The 57 delegated query logs are retained as provenance, not independently replicated searches.

regional_association.summary: The Atacama Desert is a long-standing Mars astrobiology and mineral analog, and the Namib is a Mars dune-form analog. These associations are regional. They do not establish any of the six exact 20 km footprints.

salar_atacama_jezero_specific_associatio.summary: The Cussen project page directly compares Salar de Atacama mineral maps with a synthetic model of the CRISM Jezero spectrum and with 14 Mars mineral groups. The page itself states that 12/14 Atacama equivalents are author-assigned confidence, not field-measured detections, and that r = 0.97 is against a synthetic model, not real CRISM data. The work is not peer-reviewed and its indices are pending validation. This blocks a broad claim that a Salar de Atacama-Jezero association is new, but it does not establish the exact footprint or the terrain task.

exact_footprint.summary: No public record was found for any of the six project-internal candidate IDs or their exact 20 km bounding boxes in the queried sources. The Atacama candidate lies in the broader Salar de Atacama region discussed by Cussen, and the Namib candidates lie in the broader Namib region discussed in dune literature, but no inspected source publishes these exact footprints. Absence of a match is not proof that no prior footprint record exists.

exact_task.summary: Exact task-specific association remains unresolved. Regional analogue mapping and morphology comparisons are existing research topics. Matching only a grid size, stride or identical descriptor implementation is not the criterion for scientific novelty.

novelty.summary: The audit found no exact public match in the queried sources, but this is not proof of novelty. The existing bundle claim remains appropriate: model-assisted remote-sensing assessment; no independently validated or new analogue is established.

claim_guidance: Do not describe any candidate as newly discovered, first, unique, unprecedented, or previously unassociated.
Do not claim that the exact 20 km footprints are novel; label them unresolved.
Do not claim that the four-group terrain-ranking task is novel; label it unresolved.
Do not claim peer review or independent validation for the Cussen project pages or their CAPI/CMPI indices.
Do not describe the Cussen r = 0.97 as a comparison with real CRISM data; the page says it uses a synthetic model of the Jezero spectrum.
Do not treat the 12/14 Atacama mineral equivalents as field-measured detections; the page says they are author-assigned confidence.
Use 'no public match found in the queried sources' rather than 'no prior work exists'.
Keep the regional association separate from the exact footprint and exact task claims.
evidence_limits: No peer-reviewed publication was found for the exact six footprints or the exact four-group ranking task. That is absence of evidence in the queried sources, not evidence of absence.

General web search coverage was incomplete: DuckDuckGo returned a bot challenge after the first queries; Brave returned HTTP 429; Startpage and Mojeek required JavaScript; Bing did not honor quotes and was not used as exact-string zero evidence.
OpenAlex and Crossref are bibliographic indexes with incomplete full-text coverage. Counts are tokenized and fuzzy, not exhaustive precision measures.
Candidate IDs are project-internal and have no public site names. There is no published footprint polygon to search for directly.
The Cussen pages are author project pages, not peer-reviewed publications. The CAPI/CMPI indices are proposed, pending validation, and explicitly without independent validation.
The Cussen r = 0.97 comparison uses a synthetic model of the Jezero CRISM spectrum, not real CRISM data. The 12/14 mineral equivalents are author-assigned confidence, not field-measured detections.
No paywalled full text was read. Paper assessments rely on metadata, titles, and abstracts.
The 2026 Figshare dune segmentation dataset was published 2026-11-12 and is regional; it is not evidence about the six exact footprints or the Jezero terrain-ranking task.
Project optical imagery was inspected separately but is not independent published evidence and is not used here to establish a scientific association.
No field validation, local expert consultation, or independent scientific review was performed.

The corrected v3 shortlist has four Jezero footprints and two unfilled alternative slots under 80 km context separation. The prior six-footprint audit remains archived; new western Atacama footprint only has a bounded supplementary coordinate/regional search.
coverage_gaps: Web of Science and Scopus were not available.
Spanish-language and local Chilean/Namibian literature was not systematically searched.
Mission planning documents and unindexed conference proceedings were not systematically searched.
No reverse image search or commercial satellite archive search was performed.
No systematic search of geological survey reports or national archives was performed.
